reason: Both use the same banner reflow: the headline is oversized and leaves 'fizz' alone on its own line, the subcopy is a cramped 3-line block wedged in beside the CTA, and the bottle is shrunk below the headline's weight. A also stacks both circles in the left column, so the SOLSTICE wordmark sits awkwardly across the edges of both circles and the left side looks cluttered. B keeps the original's opposite-corner circle placement, with the green circle behind the headline as a flat, deliberate layer, so it is marginally more faithful and balanced.

A: the olive circle sits directly behind 'Garden-fresh fizz', so the headline looks accidentally stacked on a shape, and the 'Find a Store' pill is shrunk to a tiny button jammed about 10px from the bottom edge, which buries the CTA. B: the headline sits cleanly on dark space and the circles are moved up as layered decoration behind the bag, but the CTA is still undersized and crowds the bottom edge, and the top-left olive circle crowds the CITRINE wordmark.

A: the headline block sits off-centre with a ragged 'Make the' line, a stray grey circle collides with the end of the shrunken 'Longest Day Sale' banner, and the legal copy is jammed inside the bottom-right circle, so the composition looks accidental. B: the headline is centred and the decorative circles sit roughly where they were in the original, but it shares A's flaws: the banner floats away from the headline, the middle-left is dead space, the body copy sits on the bottom-left circle, and the legal text is tiny and crammed into the bottom-right corner.

A: the can is shrunk to a tiny icon stuck in the lower-left, leaving a dead left-centre area. The sale ribbon floats in mid-air, nearly touching the headline's 'Make', and the legal text is set almost at CTA size, with a background dot colliding with 'Co.,'. B: the can is a better size and sits in a clearer left column, but the 'LONGEST DAY SALE' ribbon is demoted to a cramped bottom-left corner over the planet circle, which breaks the brand→sale→headline order. B has the same oversized legal block competing with the CTA.

A keeps the can on its teal circle and the headline wraps well. But the circle is clipped against the top edge, the tiny body copy is jammed against the top edge, and the three pills are scattered in a messy 2+1 cluster, with 'Summer Only' dropped alone under the CTA and almost touching the bottom. B pulls the teal circle away from the product and turns it into a logo disc behind GLACIER, so the can floats bare and tiny. Its headline breaks badly ('Mint is / back', with 'back' orphaned), and the body copy is squeezed into an illegible 6-line column of 1–2 words per line. B's stacked CTA and pills are tidier, but it loses more of the original's fidelity and typography.

The two are almost identical: the headline reflows well onto four centred lines, and the orange background, serif type and dark pill CTA are all kept. In A the CTA sits too low: there is about 130px of empty space above the headline but only about 55px below the button. The gap between headline and CTA (about 107px) is also much looser than in the original, so the button looks cut off from its message. B moves the CTA up about 10px, which tightens that gap and balances the top and bottom margins a little better. Its group is still slightly bottom-heavy, but it is closer to shippable.

Both are nearly the same stacked layout, and both share the same flaws. There is a large dead gap between the headline and the subcopy/CTA row. The flavour pills are in reverse order (Honey Rosemary first, Blood Orange last), and the legal line is illegibly small. A has comfortable ~37px margins and moves the second circle to the top-right, where it stays clear of the content; its only issue is that the top-left circle bleeds under the 'Summer' line. B squeezes everything to ~25px margins, with the CTA and Blood Orange pill almost touching the right edge. B also drops the bottom-right circle behind the Blood Orange pill, an unwanted collision that clutters the bottom corner.

A has a sensible left-to-right flow (brand, then details, then product, then CTA) and keeps the product can at a readable size. But the 'Sunset Sessions' headline is squeezed inside the circle and nearly touches the '6:00 pm' copy, the RSVP button sits in a ragged grid with badges of mismatched size, and the legal text and the missing-asset box are unreadably small. B gives the headline more weight, but its right half is badly crammed: 'Saturday 21 June' wraps into an orphaned 'June', the time and venue text is squeezed into a narrow column, the RSVP button and badges are packed tightly together, the product can is shrunk and jammed against the right edge, and the legal text is tiny. Meanwhile the left side has a lot of dead space and 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' floats on its own.

Both are crammed leaderboards. The RSVP CTA is shrunk to the size of the badge pills and buried in a 2x2 cluster, the italic tagline is squeezed into a 6–7 line column of tiny text, the legal copy is illegible, and the missing-asset placeholder still shows at the right edge. A drops the product can entirely and shrinks the Solstice logo to a near-invisible mark at far left. Its one-line headline is strong, but the brand and key imagery are lost. B keeps the logo under 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' and keeps a (tiny) can, but wraps the headline onto two smaller lines and leaves dead space around the logo.

A keeps the quote large and dominant with the attribution directly beneath it. However, the 'GROVE TASTING TEAM' line and the logo strip run into the edge of the background circle, and the logo is centred while all the text is left-aligned. The bottle sits small and off-centre in the circle, leaving the bottom-left empty. B squeezes the quote into a narrow, smaller column and pushes the attribution into an awkward side column that competes with the quote and breaks the reading order. The circle and bottle are cleanly centred, but the whole block sits on an arbitrary left indent and leaves a large dead area on the right.

A keeps the quote, quote mark and attribution together as one block and puts the can and its circle at bottom right, like the original. Its flaws: the logo floats in mid-left space with no shared edge, the attribution is nearly as heavy as the quote, and the can label is unreadably small. B squeezes the quote into a narrow five-line column with choppy breaks, drops the logo into the top-right corner where it competes with the quote, and strands the attribution at the bottom, far from its quote. The page reads as scattered fragments.

A: the SAVE 15% badge is oversized, jammed against the left edge, and pulls focus from the headline. Headline, body copy and a tiny CTA are packed into one cramped block, the coffee bag and logo shrink to icon size beside the button, and a large empty blurred photo panel wastes the right third. B: reads left to right properly (badge, then headline, then a prominent CTA at the right end). But the body copy is squeezed into a narrow column with five ragged lines and orphaned words, the bag and logo are tiny, and the blurred photo strip is meaningless filler.

A: the headline breaks as 'Box fresh, half / price', leaving 'price' orphaned on its own line. The CTA pill almost touches the right canvas edge, the box is jammed against the bottom edge, and the '48H ONLY' badge text is shrunk to illegibility. B: the headline breaks cleanly as 'Box fresh, / half price' and the CTA has a proper right margin. B still shares A's flaws: the badge text is unreadably tiny, the box crowds the bottom edge, and the striped panel is a cramped crop next to a wide lime field.

A: the plan cards are shrunk to postage stamps with illegible MONTHLY/FAMILY labels and are reordered 6-80-48, which breaks the original sequence and moves the featured yearly plan to the end. The supporting line and legal text are crammed into the right column at near-unreadable size, but the logo, headline, cards and CTA still read left to right. B has the same tiny, reordered cards. Its logo has shrunk to an illegible speck, the oversized CTA sits jammed against the top-right edge and outweighs the headline, and the subtitle, cards and legal text are stacked tightly in the centre column, so it reads as more disjointed.

A reads well as a banner (phone, then headline with its sub-copy, then CTA). Its flaws: the phone nearly touches the top and bottom edges, the headline is undersized for the canvas, the fine print is tiny, and a large dead gap separates the copy from the CTA at the far right. B scatters the pieces: the headline sits alone at the far left, away from its own fine print. The phone is jammed into the middle and also nearly touches the top and bottom edges. The '7 days free' line is orphaned below and to the left of the CTA, with no shared edge or axis, so the grouping and reading order break down.

Both cram every element of the poster into a 728x90 strip. The italic subtitle becomes an unreadable 5–7 line sliver, the legal text is tiny, the CTA pill is no bigger than the badges, and the product can is a speck. A splits the headline onto two lines but keeps the Solstice sun logo visible and the legal block apart from the placeholder. B's one-line headline is stronger, but its logo is nearly gone, its subtitle is a 7-line column jammed against 'Saturday 21 June', and its legal text collides with the red missing-asset placeholder.

A: a sensible banner split with a balanced headline break ('Box fresh, / half price'), but the 48H ONLY badge text is unreadably tiny, the box is crammed toward the bottom-left, and the CTA sits tight to the right edge. B: same left-panel problems (tiny illegible badge, box nearly touching the bottom edge), plus an orphaned 'price' on the second headline line and a CTA almost flush against the right canvas edge, which makes it feel cramped and unfinished.

A keeps the dark brand band with the logo and eyebrow intact and gives the headline clear dominance. But the CTA is shrunk to a tiny pill crammed against the legal text, and the body copy on the right is so large that it competes with the headline. B is worse: the white SOLSTICE wordmark sits on the cream background and is invisible, so the brand breaks. A leftover dark band fragment and the orange divider float in the top-right corner for no reason, the eyebrow has dropped below the body copy so the reading order is wrong, and the CTA is small and pushed to the corner.

Both use the same weak split. The oversized headline fills the lower left. Body copy, CTA and legal text are squeezed into a narrow right column with ragged centred wrapping ("Every bottle / 25% off from / sunrise to"). The legal line is set almost as large as the offer copy, which flattens the hierarchy, and the CTA is small and buried under the body copy. A also pushes the shrunken bottle against the left edge under the logo, leaving a dead empty centre. B keeps the bottle centred in the radial glow, closer to the original's focal axis. B has a minor flaw of its own: the last legal line ("Co., 2026.") runs into a background dot.

Both use the same skyscraper stack. In both, the headline breaks one word per line, the legal text is set almost as large as the '25% off' subhead, the CTA is jammed between the subhead and the legal text, and the SOLSTICE logo is tiny. In B, the rotated 'Longest Day Sale' banner and the CTA pill run almost edge to edge with no side margin, and the decorative circle crowds the phone. A keeps clean margins around the banner and the button, so A is slightly better.

A breaks the hero: the sage circle is pulled away from the can and dumped behind the body copy and the 'Find It Near You' button, which makes a collision and an orphaned blob. It also leaves big dead gaps above and below the can and shrinks the CTA to badge size. B keeps the circle and can together and reads top to bottom, but the headline block sits oddly off-centre under the centred SOLSTICE wordmark and doesn't line up with the left-aligned body copy. Its CTA is also shrunk to the same weight as the two badges in one row, so the call to action gets lost.

Both use the same banner split: a big headline on the left, and on the right a narrow column where the subcopy wraps into five ragged centred lines ('Solstice / botanical / ...') and sits jammed against the top and right edges, with the button nearly touching the bottom edge. A is slightly worse: its headline runs from a tiny left margin until its final period almost touches the subcopy column. B's slightly smaller headline leaves a bit more left margin and a clearer gutter, but the right column is equally cramped.

Both cram the headline into a 4-line block that nearly fills the canvas, with a tight top margin. Both also break the original's centred stack: the subline is pushed bottom-left and wraps awkwardly ('Now in four / flavours.') beside a small CTA whose label is close to too small to read. A has slightly more breathing room. B's larger headline and CTA run closer to the right edge (CTA about 10px from it), so B looks more cramped.

The two are almost identical. Both centre the headline well, but they move 'Now in four flavours.' off the headline and set it beside the CTA in a bottom footer row, where it wraps to two lines with 'flavours.' alone on the second. They also leave a large empty band between the headline and the footer, and the footer row is not centred on the headline's axis. B's button sits about 17px from the right edge, against about 26px in A, and its row is lower and more cramped, so A has slightly better margins.

Both split the LIMITED badge from its CTA and leave it floating at the right, which breaks the original's grouping. Both also shrink the 'See the Flavours' button until it is tiny next to the oversized headline and push it against the bottom edge. B is slightly worse: its headline nearly touches the left and right canvas edges, and its button and badge sit even closer to the bottom. A keeps a little more margin.

A keeps the bottle-on-cream-circle motif, but the headline floats top-centre on no shared edge with the bottle or buttons. NEW and Try It sit in a loose mid-row with a big dead band above them, and the faint decorative circle is clipped at the top-left corner. B breaks the key motif: the cream circle is left orphaned and clipped in the bottom-left corner while an oversized bottle stands alone mid-canvas. The headline runs almost into the bottle, and the NEW/Try It column on the right is disconnected from the headline, which leaves the layout scattered.

Both squeeze the poster into a 320x50 strip. In both, the description and venue copy render at about 4px, which is unreadable. The logo mark is gone, the RSVP CTA has shrunk into a tiny pill or a line of fine print, and the pills, body copy and date compete as one cramped cluster. B is worse because it also carries the original's grey/red placeholder box into the lower right, where it jams against the body text and the canvas edge.

A keeps the original's offset circle bleeding off the bottom-right corner, but the quote sits cramped against the top edge, the yellow attribution is oversized and nearly competes with the quote, and the logo is centred under the attribution while the copy is flush left. B makes the same text mistakes (oversized attribution, a logo floating at an arbitrary x that matches neither the left edge nor the text centre). It also squeezes a full circle behind the can that almost touches the top and bottom edges, which looks cramped and drops the original's corner-bleed composition.

Both use the same reasonable left-to-right banner structure, with the quote mark, the 3-line headline and the attribution on the left and the can on the right. Both share the same flaw: the logo floats alone in the middle gap instead of anchoring a corner or grouping with anything. A: the backing circle is pushed off-centre down and to the right of the can, which reads as misplaced rather than as the original's deliberate cropped corner arc, and the can's sun icon crowds the top edge. B: centring the can on a complete circle reads as an intentional product badge and balances the right side better, though the full disc drifts from the original's corner arc and the sun icon still sits tight to the top edge.

A keeps the right hierarchy: the quote is the dominant element, the attribution is clearly secondary, and the purple circle stays behind the can as in the original. Its flaws are a quote block that runs almost to the right edge, the attribution packed tightly under the quote, and a tiny logo jammed against the bottom edge just under the can. B gets the hierarchy backwards: the attribution 'THE ULTRA TASTING TEAM' is set larger and heavier than the quote itself, and the quote is shrunk. B also moves the purple circle up behind the quote mark, which breaks its link to the product and turns it into a stray shape in the corner, and its quote line 'gone too soon.' crowds the right edge.

A turns the layout into a clean two-column banner: the can sits centered in a full circle with the logo grouped under it. But the quote is squeezed into a narrow 4-line column with a weak 'a' line-end, the attribution is jammed right under the quote, there is a large dead gap below the quote mark, and the circle crowds the top edge. B gets the quote line length right (3 lines), but the purple circle is pushed off to the bottom-right, so the can's top half floats on the plain background and only its bottom overlaps the circle edge. That misregistration looks accidental, and the logo straddles the circle edge, which weakens the original's deliberate product-in-circle motif.

The two are almost the same skyscraper reflow: the headline and copy stack well and the CTA is clear. In both, the VOLTSTRIDE box straddles the hard edge between the stripes and the green panel, which looks accidental, and the box is shrunk to a minor element. The headline and body text also run almost edge to edge with very thin side margins. B is slightly worse: its larger badge nearly touches the box, crowding the top, and its wider CTA pill sits closer to the canvas edges.

Both use the same weak banner structure. The eyebrow '24 HOURS, 24 / READERS' breaks awkwardly and is set so large it competes with the headline. The legal line is crammed into an unreadably small column at the far right. The book cover is pushed against the top and left edges, and the logo, eyebrow and body copy sit in staggered blocks that share no edge. A is slightly worse because its body copy leaves 'night.' alone on the last line. B wraps the body copy into three balanced lines, but its CTA is smaller and floats further from the copy it belongs to.

The two are almost the same 160x600 skyscraper, and they share the same flaws. The headline breaks one or two words per line ('Make / the / longest / day / last') and crowds out the phone. The legal fine print is set nearly as large as the '25% off' line and runs four lines, pushed against the CTA and the bottom edge. The SOLSTICE logo is shrunk to an illegible speck. A is slightly worse: its sun icon is almost invisible, and its CTA button runs nearly edge to edge with no side margin. B keeps a slightly more visible logo mark and a CTA inset a little from the edges.

A separates the cream circle from the bottle and leaves it as a meaningless half-cropped blob in the bottom-left corner, under a stray top-left circle. The bottle sits in a crowded middle and the headline floats at mid-left with no shared edge, so the brand motif is broken. B keeps the bottle-in-circle motif and a clear left-to-right row (product, NEW, Try It), but the headline is off-centre and lines up with nothing. NEW and Try It float far apart with uneven gutters, and there is wasted space on the right.

A keeps the headline on one line with a clear left/right split (logo, can and circle up top, copy and CTA below), but the can is small and jammed into the top-right circle, and the two-line body copy is very small and sits on the peach circle. B wraps the headline so 'fizz' is left alone on its own line, and that oversized headline overwhelms the shrunken can, which is pushed against the top edge. B's CTA label is tiny inside an oversized button and its body copy is a cramped three-line block, which is weaker hierarchy and typography than A.

A reads left to right in a sensible order (product, headline, CTA), but the product is shrunk to an unreadable sliver and the CITRINE logo under the CTA is microscopic, so the brand is effectively lost; the decorative circles are also gone. B keeps a legible logo, but its 'Find a Store' CTA is a tiny, illegible pill buried at the far left before the headline, the product is a speck in the middle, and the left cluster is cramped while the headline floats alone, so the hierarchy and reading order are broken.

A: the headline leads, but the body copy column is so large it competes with the headline. The 'Reserve a Case' CTA is shrunk to a tiny pill and the legal text is unreadable. The dark header bar survives only as a stray black sliver at top right, with an orphan rule line above the logo. B has all of A's flaws, and the leftover dark bar also covers and cuts off the first line of body copy ('Each bottle is filled by'). Its headline's last line also runs almost into the body column.

A: the logo has lost its white band and sits dark-on-navy at the far left, so it is nearly invisible. The 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow is gone, and the body copy is squeezed into a narrow 5-line column of tiny text beside the CTA. The order still reads cleanly: headline, then copy, then button, then 'Ships late June'. B has the same invisible dark-on-navy logo. The eyebrow is stranded at the bottom-left, far from the headline. The body copy is jammed against the top edge, the CTA is pushed to the bottom edge, and 'Ships late June' is crushed into an illegible sliver beside the button, so the right side is badly cramped.

Both candidates share the same core flaws. The 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow is shrunk to unreadable micro-type and moved below the headline, which flips the reading order. The body copy is set almost as large as the headline, so the two compete for attention, and the text runs as a long, heavy column. In A, the dark header band is shrunk to a sliver and the SOLSTICE logo and wordmark become specks, so the brand all but disappears; the orange divider is also gone. B keeps a slightly taller header with a legible wordmark and keeps the orange divider, though it moves the divider above the headline. That makes B a little better on brand, but it is still not shippable.

A: the bottom is cramped into a three-column row. The subcopy is squeezed into a narrow 4-line column, and the legal text is a tiny, ragged 7-line column jammed beside the CTA. The bottle floats off-axis on the left with dead space to its right, and the logo and ribbon sit at unrelated heights. B: keeps a clear centered top-to-bottom reading order with a strong CTA. But the headline orphans 'last' on its own line, the legal text is promoted above the CTA almost as large as the subcopy (and orphans 'Co., 2026.'), and the logo floats at an arbitrary right-of-center spot instead of sharing an edge with the ribbon.

A keeps the can inside its circle and wraps the headline cleanly, but the right cluster is jammed: the body copy touches the top edge, and the CTA and badges are scattered (SUMMER ONLY sits orphaned below, off the grid), with tiny text throughout. B separates the can from its circle and reuses the empty circle as a backing for the SOLSTICE wordmark, which overflows it. Its headline breaks awkwardly ('Mint is / back'), and the body copy is squeezed into a narrow 7-line column of illegible text. B's stacked CTA and badges are tidier, but the brand imagery is mangled.

A keeps the headline dominant and the product inside its circle. But the product shrinks to a small bottom-left vignette that spills past its circle. The CTA sits at the top of the right stack, above the badges, which jumbles the reading order. The body copy is jammed against the bottom edge. B breaks the main visual: the green circle is left empty behind the GROVE wordmark, and the product is cut down to a tiny detached icon in the top-right corner. The headline also runs over the circle's edge. The body copy is shrunk to near-illegible fine print, and the stacked pills crowd the right side.

Both reflow the headline well into four centred lines, but both break the original grouping. The LIMITED badge is moved to the right of the CTA and floats loose. The CTA row is left-weighted under a centred headline, so the axis is incoherent, and both sit in a cramped band near the bottom. A is slightly worse: its headline nearly touches the side edges and its CTA sits only about 25px from the left edge, while B keeps slightly more comfortable margins.

Both use the same weak structure. The 'Shop Flavours' button is oversized and competes with the headline. The flavour pills are out of the original order, with Blood Orange orphaned on a second row. The right side is a cramped cluster, with legal text jammed into the peach circle. The headline's 'here' nearly touches the Honey Rosemary pill. B adds an inconsistent pill style: Blood Orange uses much smaller text than the other two pills. B also has tighter edge margins (headline at about 15px from the left, tagline and legal text nearly touching the right edge), so A is slightly less broken.

A reads cleanly left to right (headline, copy, product in its peach circle, CTA with legal underneath), but the 'WEEKEND ONLY' kicker is jammed against the top edge, the three-line body copy is so big it competes with the headline, and the legal line is microscopic. B has the same kicker problem, plus the Shop Sale button runs right up to the right canvas edge with no margin, the legal text wraps awkwardly onto two tiny lines pressed against the bottom, and the can is small and floats without its circle, so the right side looks cramped and unresolved.

A has a clean vertical stack with a strong headline, but the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow has moved below the body copy, so the reading order is wrong. It also mixes alignments: the text is left-aligned while the bottle and CTA are centred. The body copy leaves 'sparkling.' alone on its own line, and there is dead space at the top. B squeezes the body copy into a narrow column with one to two words per line ('Every / mixed / case of'). It also wraps the eyebrow onto two cramped lines jammed beside the headline, and the oversized bottle takes over the canvas, so the headline is no longer the main focal point.

A: the cream circle sits behind the start of the white headline, so 'Blood' nearly disappears; the bottle is pulled out of its circle and floats between the headline and the CTA; and the NEW pill overlaps the Try It button. B: the headline sits cleanly on orange and reads well, and bottle and circle stay together, but the circle rams into the 't' of 'Sunset' with no gap, the NEW pill is jammed onto the top of the button, and the right side is cramped against the edge.

A breaks reading order: the 'Solstice Tasting Team' attribution sits above the quote, in a right-shifted column that doesn't line up with the quote. The quote is squeezed into a narrow column with choppy 2–3-word lines, and the logo is too small to read. B keeps the order and gives the quote a wider, cleaner wrap, but the attribution is pushed to the very bottom at a tiny, unreadable size, far from its quote. B's logo is also microscopic, there is dead space under the quote mark, and the backdrop circle is awkwardly cropped behind the can. B is slightly less broken.

A: the attribution 'THE SOLSTICE TASTING TEAM' is pulled out into a separate right-hand column level with the quote, so it competes with the quote instead of sitting under it. The SOLSTICE logo floats mid-canvas between the quote and the can, lined up with neither, and the can sits off-centre at the edge of its circle, which looks accidental. B makes the same attribution split, and the logo sitting centred under left-aligned text looks arbitrary. But the attribution reads as deliberate inside the lilac circle, the can is centred on its maroon circle, and the quote block is tighter. The big empty lower-right corner is still a flaw.

Both use the same banner reflow: stripes on the left, then the box, headline, and subcopy stacked above the CTA on the right. Their flaws are similar: the box straddles the stripe/lime seam awkwardly, and the 48H badge is tiny and jammed against the left edge. A's badge is partly clipped at the left edge, and its CTA pill crowds the right edge. B's box corner overlaps the pink badge, an unwanted collision, though B leaves a better right margin. I picked A by a slim margin because a clean badge beats a collision.

A shrinks the Enter Now CTA and the LIMITED badge to unreadable specks under the tiny shoe. That buries the call to action, and the three-line subcopy on the right ends up competing with the headline. B keeps the CTA as a legible lime pill, but the LIMITED badge is now as large as the CTA and competes with it. B's subcopy wraps awkwardly, leaving 'Thursday.' alone on its own line, the headline is jammed against the left edge, and the shoe is shrunk to an icon, so B still needs fixes before it could ship.

A: the logo lost its white band and is now dark on navy, so it is almost invisible. The 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow is tiny and cut off from the headline, and the body copy and the 'Ships late June' note are crammed into a corner at the far right, too small to read. Its CTA is at least big and clear. B: the logo is still faint and the eyebrow is reduced to a stray orange rule. The CTA is a cramped little pill with tiny text, so it loses to the six-line body block next to it, though 'Ships late June' is readable.

Both use the same structure: a big centred headline, then the CTA pushed left and the LIMITED badge drifting off on its own to the right. That breaks the centred axis and the original's tight badge-and-button group, and the badge has swapped sides. B is slightly worse because its headline runs closer to the side edges and its CTA sits only about 25px from the left edge, which looks jammed; A keeps a little more margin all round.

A: the headline reads cleanly on the orange. But the bottle and its cream circle are jammed against the 't' of 'Sunset' with no gap, and the NEW pill is stacked onto the top edge of the Try It button, which looks cramped rather than planned. B: the cream circle is left behind 'Blood', so the white 'B' sits on cream with almost no contrast (a text collision that hurts legibility). The bottle has lost its circle and floats on its own, and B has the same cramped NEW/Try It stacking.

Both rebuild the design as a sensible left-to-right leaderboard: striped strip, then the box, the headline and the CTA. In both, the box sticks out over the stripe/lime boundary and the subcopy is tiny at 90px tall. A's subcopy breaks awkwardly ('every / size still in stock'). B fixes that line break, but its pink badge sinks almost to the bottom edge, its bigger box crowds the headline, and its CTA is jammed close to the right edge, so A is slightly better balanced.

A keeps the 'Enter Now' CTA legible and the headline strong. However, the LIMITED badge is blown up to the CTA's size and competes with it, the shoe is shrunk to a tiny icon, and the body copy wraps awkwardly ('closes / Thursday.') into the top-right corner. B's single-line headline works, but the CTA and LIMITED pills are shrunk to unreadable slivers under the shoe, which buries the action. Its three-line body copy is also jammed against the right edge.

A keeps a clean centered column and the original hierarchy, but the SOLSTICE wordmark is clipped by the bottom of the shortened header band. The headline, body and CTA are separated by big uneven dead gaps, and the legal text is microscopic. B is worse: the header band floats about 55px down with an empty cream strip above it, and the eyebrow is jammed into the header. The body copy and CTA drift left of the centered headline's axis, so the alignment looks ragged and arbitrary, and B has the same large dead gaps.

A: the right-hand cluster is overstuffed. The FREE DELIVERY badge collides with the tiny product image, the CTA is a speck no bigger than the pills, the body copy can't be read at 320x50, and the circle backdrop is gone. Still, it reads in order: GROVE, headline, product, action. B has the same overstuffed cluster with the same badge/product collision and unreadable body copy.
